text.p: The following are the main stories from Tuesday's Albanian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- The newspaper editorial says there is a friction between the United States and the European Union concerning Albania, with some European states supporting the ruling Democratic Party and President Sali Berisha during the current crisis.
- Student hunger strikers in the southern town of Vlore fear the secret police SHIK is trying to disrupt their strike. Students from other universities support them with telegrams.
- Berisha is doing his utmost to work towards his re-election as president while there is speculation some members of parliament may create obstacles to his re-election.
- The Forum for Democracy opposition grouping called on the ruling Democratic Party not to choose Berisha as its presidential candidate.
- Forum for Democracy is not showing the proper reaction to the current crisis in the country, a commentary says.
- Lek, the Albanian currency, is being rapidly devalued.
- Organisers of the Miss Europe 1996 beauty pageant deny they received money from the bankrupt pyramid investment scheme Gjallica.

- The lek is significantly devalued, banks increase their interest rates with many Albanians rushing to exchange the capital reimbursed from failed pyramid investment schemes into hard currency, a newspaper editorial says.
- The southern town of Kucove held its 13th successive daily protest supporting the Vlore hunger strike.
- European Union foreign minister called on Albania to start dialogue and respect democratic principles.
